newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore HSFO seen soft, pressured by high stocks.
newsitem.headline: Singapore HSFO seen soft, pressured by high stocks.

text.p: High sulphur fuel oil prices on Thursday were expected to soften as weak fundamentals would offset any gains in crude, traders said.
The prompt December contract on ACCESS gained 22 cents to be last traded at $24.50 per barrel.
But fundamentals remained weak in Asia with ample supplies from Thailand, Kuwait and South Korea.
Cargo 180-cst prices were quoted at $117-$119 per tonne on Thursday.
Traders said prices were likely to hover between $116-$118 per tonne Thursday.
Traders said high inventories are also putting pressure on prices.
Singapore weekly residues stocks were up by 739,000 barrels to reach 11.373 million barrels, according to the Trade Development Board of Singapore.
In the swaps market, November paper was discussed at $117.50/$118.50, little changed from Wednesday.
